title: Hotfix: recover severe tokens/sec collapse for mixed-model multiplexing
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and several Private installs reported a sudden ~60-80% drop in sustained tokens/sec for long-lived multiplexed workers that serve mixed-model traffic (small-chat + mid-sized instruction-tuned models). First-token latency also regressed for those workers. Impact was most visible on high-concurrency tenant pools and during steady-state traffic following model warmups.

Observed behavior:
- Drop in tokens/sec and increased first-token latency (FTL) starting ~2026-03-13 02:40 UTC on several regions.
- Issue manifests only for multiplexed workers that simultaneously host models from different kernel families (e.g., attention kernel A vs kernel B) and where per-request sequence length variance is high.
- CPU-side scheduler shows rapid kernel-selection churn and frequent KV cache eviction/rehydration cycles. GPU-side memory copy and kernel relaunch overheads spike, causing serialization between streams and throughput collapse.

Hypothesis: A recent kernel selector heuristic change (release runtime-2.4.0) introduced a cost-recalculation path that runs per-request when mixed-model dispatch patterns are detected. Under multiplexed loads this triggered frequent kernel reselection and forced KV cache invalidation in shared worker processes. The combination leads to excessive host<->device work and scheduler contention, hurting tokens/sec and FTL.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix plan):
1) Canary rollback of the kernel-selector dynamic recalculation to the pre-2.4.0 heuristic for multiplexed worker pools — deploy to two Hosted canaries and one Dedicated canary.
2) Apply an emergency worker config change to enable strict per-model affinity (worker-level isolation flag) for multiplexing-sensitive pools to prevent cross-model KV reuse interference.
3) Apply transient throttling on new model warmups in multiplexed pools (limit concurrent warmups to 1 per worker) to avoid simultaneous kernel transitions.
4) Patch the kernel-selector code to memoize per-model kernel decisions for the duration of a request batch and avoid per-request re-evaluation (short-term code path, unit-tested).
5) Notify Private customers with upgrade windows and provide an opt-in lightweight hotpatch for air-gapped installs.

Verification and roll-forward criteria:
- After canary deploy, tokens/sec should return to baseline within 10 minutes for canary pools and FTL should drop by >=50% relative to the spike.
- Telemetry queries: tokens/sec over 5min windows, mean first-token latency over 1min windows, kernel-selection rate metric, KV cache miss rate.
- If canary stable for 30m, roll to remaining Hosted and Dedicated pools in staged fashion (region by region).

Rollback plan: Re-enable runtime-2.4.0 heuristic and revert affinity flag to previous config if any adverse regressions observed (increase in overall GPU memory or unexpected memory fragmentation).

Follow-ups (post-hotfix):
- Deep postmortem to root-cause the regression in detail and add unit/integration tests to prevent future kernel-selector churn regressions.
- Add an automated alert that detects spikes in kernel-selection rate and KV eviction frequency and ties them to customer-facing tokens/sec impact.
- Design a longer-term fix that allows dynamic kernel decisions but avoids per-request churn (caching, lightweight epoch-based invalidation).

Affected customers: multiple Hosted tenants on prod-us-west-2 and two Dedicated customers in EU with high multiplex ratios. Private customers on v1.9 and v2.2 installs may need manual patching.

Links to artifacts: see links field for PRs, dashboards, confluence notes and runbooks.
